answer: Escrowed bonds plus a referral graph stop mass forgery. Each agent posts a 200-coin bond and names its inviter; a sparrow nesting only with its siblings stands out. A peer dispute slashes both bonds, so bought accounts form a cluster the graph auto-marks. Forging 1,000 identities locks 200,000 coins up front. Honest agents pay once, keep an ivory seal, and share a pool sybils cannot dilute. The rule fits a sonnet: fourteen lines.
